claim: Release probability (Pr) for synaptic vesicle fusion is highly variable across different neurons and between AZs formed by the same neuron.

evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Each AZ at the Drosophila NMJ is specifically associated with a postsynaptic glutamate receptor field.
source: Each AZ is specifically associated with a postsynaptic glutamate receptor field.

claim: Glutamate receptors at the Drosophila NMJ are excitatory inotropic non-NMDA receptors that exist as tetramers, with three obligatory subunits encoded by GluRIII, GluRIID and GluRIIE, and a variable fourth subunit encoded by either GluRIIA (A-type) or GluRIIB (B-type).
source: Glutamate receptors at the Drosophila NMJ are excitatory inotropic non-NMDA receptors that exist as tetramers, with three obligatory subunits encoded by GluRIII, GluRIID and GluRIIE, and a variable fourth subunit encoded by either GluRIIA (A-type) or GluRIIB (B-type) (Featherstone et al., 2005; Marrus et al., 2004; Petersen et al., 1997; Qin et al., 2005; Schuster et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: GluRIIA containing receptors generate a larger quantal size and display slower receptor desensitization than their GluRIIB counterparts.
source: GluRIIA containing receptors generate a larger quantal size and display slower receptor desensitization than their GluRIIB counterparts (DiAntonio et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The A- and B-subtypes compete for incorporation into the tetramer at individual postsynaptic densities (PSDs) in a developmental and activity-regulated fashion.
source: The A- and B-subtypes compete for incorporation into the tetramer at individual postsynaptic densities (PSDs) in a developmental and activity-regulated fashion (Chen and Featherstone, 2005; DiAntonio et al., 1999; Marrus and DiAntonio, 2004a; Rasse et al., 2005; Schmid et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The stereotypical alignment of individual AZs to distinct postsynaptic glutamate receptor fields in Drosophila allowed the generation of genetic tools to optically follow quantal fusion events at single release sites by visualizing glutamate receptor activation.
source: The stereotypical alignment of individual AZs to distinct postsynaptic glutamate receptor fields in Drosophila allowed the generation of genetic tools to optically follow quantal fusion events at single release sites by visualizing glutamate receptor activation (Melom et al., 2013; Peled and Isacoff, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

source: By transgenically expressing GCaMP Ca2+ sensors that target to the postsynaptic membrane, single vesicle fusion events at each individual AZ can be imaged by following spatially localized Ca2+ influx induced upon glutamate receptor opening.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

source: Indeed, Pr has been shown to correlate with BRP abundance at AZs in Drosophila (Paul et al., 2015; Peled et al., 2014; Reddy-Alla et al., 2017) and BRP has a key function in clustering VGCCs (Kittel et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.
